label: Contingent joint condition versus necessity of its individual sources
term: contingent joint condition versus necessity of its individual sources
resolution: A conjunction of fact conditions is true only when all its fixed members hold. Contingency of that conjunction does not imply contingency of every member, and does not remove any necessary individual in the original ontology. An existential alternative among different sufficient groups is not this conjunction. Necessary existence of a source is not necessity of its action; an existence-condition roster is not automatically a jointly sufficient productive cause. No new group substance, cause-of-the-group law, explanation distribution or fact-to-being identification is imported.
